tasks.task: Establish site, scaffold access, and occupant interface
tasks.scope: Mobilise plant and materials. Set up scaffold access via Kiora Lane and courtyard. Brief occupants on exclusion zones, noise, dust, and edge hazard below balconies. Establish site rules and emergency contacts.
hazards: Trip hazard from plant, materials, and temporary works during mobilisation
Struck-by hazard from moving plant and delivery vehicles in courtyard and Kiora Lane
Communication failure with occupants leading to unauthorised access to exclusion zones
Noise and dust exposure to neighbouring occupants and construction staff

Appoint site traffic controller to direct all deliveries and plant movements; controller wears high-visibility clothing and communicates via two-way radio to all operators.
Mark all pedestrian walkways with yellow-and-black hazard tape; identify exclusion zones below scaffold and balconies with signage and barricading.
Brief all site workers on plant movement routes, exclusion zones, and emergency stop procedure before work starts.
Brief occupants in writing on construction hours, noise levels, dust control measures, and exclusion zones; obtain signed acknowledgment from each occupied unit.
Provide occupants with emergency contact numbers and site supervisor mobile; post contact numbers in common areas and lifts.
Conduct pre-mobilisation walk with scaffolder and supervisor to confirm access route, set-down areas, material staging, and handover points.
Verify scaffold erection permit is signed by licenced scaffolder and displayed on site before scaffold erection starts.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to balconies and install edge protection
tasks.scope: Erect scaffold over 4m to all affected balconies per engineer design and certifier approval. Install edge protection, guardrails, and working platforms. Confirm load capacity and stability. Install exclusion signage and barriers below active edges.

Structural failure or collapse of scaffold due to defective components or poor fixing
Fall of materials or tools from height onto occupants or construction staff below
Instability of scaffold on uneven or damaged bearing surfaces
Entanglement or crush hazard during guardrail and platform installation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from scaffold platform during erection and dismantling
controls: Confirm engineer design and load calculations match site bearing surfaces and building structure before any scaffold component arrives on site.
check all scaffold components for damage, corrosion, or missing pins before erection — reject defective parts immediately.
Check bearing surfaces are level, solid, and load-bearing — remove debris, water, or loose material — document photographs before work starts.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: Site supervisor, licenced scaffolder, and building manager confirm bearing surfaces are prepared and acceptable.
Install base plates and standards vertically using spirit level — do not proceed if surface is uneven or cracked.
Secure all scaffold connections — pins, bolts, and ledger-to-building bonds — using documented torque specifications from engineer design.
Tie scaffold to building structure at intervals specified by engineer — use only anchor points approved by building owner or structural consultant.
Install guardrails and edge protection to all open edges as you build — do not leave any platform edge unprotected during or after erection.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: Site supervisor, licenced scaffolder, and building manager confirm bearing surfaces are prepared and acceptable.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto completed scaffold until: Scaffold certifier issues handover certificate and load-capacity plate is installed and visible.

🛑 STOP WORK if: Bearing surface subsides, shifts, or shows signs of failure — recheck level and load capacity before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Guardrail or edge protection is incomplete, damaged, or removed — do not access that section until repaired and approved.

tasks.task: Remove existing membrane, screed, tile bed, and sealants
tasks.scope: Strip , screed, and tile bed from all balconies. Remove sealants and fittings. Dispose as per waste classification. Manage silica dust during screed removal. Leave substrate bare and safe for inspection

Cut or laceration from broken tiles and sharp debris
Struck-by hazard from falling tile fragments and debris during removal
Dust and debris ingestion or eye irritation
Sealant chemical exposure during removal and disposal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Silica dust inhalation from screed removal and grinding
controls: Wet suppression — spray screed and tile bed with water mist before any removal to prevent dust release; maintain damp state throughout removal work
Install local dust extraction at point of removal — attach shroud to hand grinder or cutting tool and connect to HEPA-filtered dust extractor; run continuously during grinding or cutting
Use hand tools (chisels, pry bars) in preference to power tools where practicable; where power tools are required, operate with extraction shroud fitted and wet suppression active

Erect full-height exclusion barrier around work area — barricade with shade cloth and signage to prevent public and occupants walking through or below; segregate removed debris in skip or sealed bags on site
Wear organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) when removing sealants; wear P100 particulate respirator (or higher) when generating dust from screed or tiles despite wet suppression
Wear cut-resistant gloves and rigger boots; wear eye protection

Bag all broken tiles and sealant fragments immediately in labelled waste bags; label each bag with material type and destination; segregate asbestos-free declaration or hazmat declaration per waste classification

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove sealants until: [named consultant] confirms sealant material type, hazard classification, and ventilation requirement from SDS

🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extractor is disconnected, damaged, or no longer operating; do not resume until extractor is checked and confirmed working
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion barrier is breached or public/occupants enter work zone
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Expose substrate and document condition
tasks.scope: Clean substrate of loose material and dust. Photograph all visible cracks, spalling, and slab movement. Mark defects and measure crack widths. Prepare condition report for Leo and Associates inspection.
hazards: Dust and debris inhalation during substrate cleaning and vacuuming
Trip hazard from loose concrete, spalling fragments, and cleaning equipment
Exposure to unstable or weakened substrate surfaces during inspection and photography
Manual handling injury while moving cleaning equipment and documentation materials
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust and debris inhalation during substrate cleaning and vacuuming
controls: Vacuum all loose concrete debris and dust using HEPA-filtered equipment before any manual cleaning or inspection starts.
Wet wipe substrate surface with damp cloth to suppress residual dust — do not dry sweep or air-blast.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and function-checked before starting vacuuming or manual cleaning work.
Clear spalling fragments and loose material into labelled waste container — do not drop or kick debris onto lower levels or occupied areas.
Photograph cracks and spalling in-situ using macro lens — position equipment to avoid trip hazards on scaffold surface.
Mark crack locations with non-permanent pen and measure widths with ruler or caliper — record dimensions directly on photo or condition log.
Barricade or guard any substrate edge or void that cannot be repaired or bridged within this task — use edge protection tape or foam guard.
Do not walk or kneel directly on visibly spalled or weakened substrate areas — use scaffold platform or protective board if access required.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next remedial task until: Leo and Associates has received and signed off condition report and approved remedial method for identified defects.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition reveals load-bearing structural damage, significant slab movement, or failure not anticipated in scope — tell Site Manager and wait for engineer assessment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA vacuum fails mid-task or P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) cannot maintain seal — resume only after equipment replacement and function check.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupied areas below scaffold are not effectively excluded from dust and debris fall during cleaning — implement additional dust sheet or containment before resuming.

tasks.scope: Fill and repair slab cracks, spalling, and concrete defects per Leo and Associates specification. Grind, clean, and prepare repair surfaces. Apply appropriate repair mortar or epoxy. make sure repaired substrate is sound, stable, and suitable for membrane bonding.

Noise exposure from grinding and surface preparation work

tasks.task: Apply waterproofing membrane system to prepared slab
tasks.scope: Prime substrate per system specification. Apply waterproofing membrane (liquid or sheet) to all balcony areas including slab, upstands, and perimeter. Lap and seal all joints and penetrations per manufacturer and engineer detail. Cure and test per specification.
hazards: Chemical inhalation or skin contact from waterproofing membrane primer, solvents, or adhesives
Slip and fall hazard from wet or slippery membrane application on elevated balcony surfaces
Chemical burn from membrane products or primers
Fume inhalation in enclosed or poorly ventilated balcony spaces during application and curing
Fall from height during application of sheet or liquid membrane to vertical upstands
tasks.dominant_hazard: Chemical inhalation or skin contact from waterproofing membrane primer, solvents, or adhesives
controls: Obtain Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for membrane primer and product. Review Section 8 (Exposure controls) and Section 16 (Other information) on point of use before mixing or application.

Establish continuous natural cross-ventilation or mechanical ventilation (minimum 6 air changes per hour) across balcony and adjacent enclosed spaces before application starts. Close windows and doors only if positive pressure ventilation is confirmed active.
Apply substrate priming and membrane in calm, dry conditions (wind speed ≤20 km/h, no rain forecast within cure window per SDS). Do not start application if weather cannot support full cure cycle.
Wear organic vapour respirator (cartridge type per SDS Section 8 requirements), chemical-resistant gloves, and hi-viz shirt or vest
Confirm substrate is dry, sound, and free of dust or contamination per engineer specification before priming. Do not prime if substrate is damp or frost-covered.

Designate primer and membrane application zone as exclusion area. Post 'Chemical Application — No Entry' signs at all access points. Restrict occupants to minimum distance specified in SDS or 10 m, whichever is greater.

Apply primer and membrane in thin, even coats per manufacturer specification. Do not over-apply or pool product on horizontal surfaces. Apply coats only within recommended temperature and humidity range (check SDS Section 7).
Seal all joints, laps, and penetrations immediately after membrane sets (per manufacturer cure time — typically 24–48 hours). Do not allow bare laps or joints to remain exposed overnight.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not prime substrate until: SDS and engineer detail reviewed on site, continuous ventilation confirmed active, and substrate condition checked and signed off by Site Supervisor or Waterproofing Contractor lead hand.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit foot traffic or load exposure until: full cure time per manufacturer specification (documented in SDS Section 2.1 or technical data sheet) has elapsed and Site Supervisor has confirmed cure completion.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails, smoke or visible fumes appear indoors, or occupants report respiratory symptoms during or immediately after application.

🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition differs from engineer specification (soft, wet, contaminated, or unstable), or if weather conditions cannot support required cure window (temperature drop, rain, humidity >85%).
🛑 STOP WORK if: chemical burn incident, respiratory distress, or skin reaction occurs. Initiate first aid, contact emergency services if required, and isolate affected worker.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Apply screed and reinstate tile finish to balconies
tasks.scope: Apply levelling screed to waterproofing membrane with fall toward drainage. Lay floor tiles and grout per architect detail. Set and seal all tile joints. make sure fall and drainage function correctly. Allow cure time before trafficked.
hazards: Slip and fall from wet or freshly laid screed on elevated balcony surfaces
Cut or laceration from tile edges and cutting tools during tile laying
Repetitive strain injury from grouting and tile laying activities
Chemical contact or inhalation from tile adhesive, grout, and sealant fumes
Back or muscle strain from manual handling of tiles, screed, and materials
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip and fall from wet or freshly laid screed on elevated balcony surfaces
controls: Lay non-slip matting or anti-slip tape over screed fall zone before application start; keep in place until screed cures and tiles are laid.
Apply screed in shallow sections; do not extend beyond working area or create trip edges.
Establish wet work exclusion zone on balcony perimeter — barricade and delineate with safety tape; no entry except tiler and assistant.
check waterproofing membrane for defects, ponding, or contamination before screed application; document condition; stop work if membrane is damaged.
Wear rubber-soled steel-capped footwear; change or clean boots if soles become slippery or caked with screed residue.
Use tile spacers and setting gauges to maintain consistent bed thickness; check fall gradient with level at completion to confirm drainage fall.
Score or cut tiles only over designated cutting area away from wet surfaces; collect all tile shards and bag for disposal immediately.
Mix grout and adhesive in batches only; discard unused material after 4 hours or per SDS guidance; cover open containers to prevent skin contact or inhalation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: waterproofing membrane is inspected and signed off by supervising tradesperson, fall gradient is confirmed, and exclusion zone is fully barricaded.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or reinstate balcony use until: grout cure time is complete per manufacturer SDS, sealant has hardened, and drainage function is tested by pouring water and observing flow toward outlets.

🛑 STOP WORK if: waterproofing membrane is found to be damaged, has pooling water, or substrate is contaminated; do not proceed until membrane is repaired and re-approved.
🛑 STOP WORK if: chemical fumes from adhesive, grout, or sealant cause dizziness, headache, or breathing difficulty; evacuate balcony and ventilate before resuming.

Chemical exposure from flexible sealant application and curing fumes

task_blocks_raw.task: Clean, reinstate occupant access, and brief final handover
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove site debris and protection. Reinstate occupant access to balconies and common areas. Brief occupants on curing time, maintenance requirements, and any restricted use periods. Leave site clean and safe.
hazards: Trip hazard from debris, residual material, and cleaning equipment during site clean-up
Dust inhalation during final clean-up and removal of temporary protection systems
Communication failure with occupants leading to premature access to unsafe areas during cure periods
Struck-by hazard from removal of temporary barriers and protection systems
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Trip hazard from debris, residual material, and cleaning equipment during site clean-up
controls: Clear all debris, residual material, and dust from balconies and common areas before reinstating occupant access.
Use damp wiping or HEPA vacuum to remove silica dust from horizontal surfaces and ledges — do not dry sweep.
Lay dust sheets or cordon off work areas during final clean-up to prevent dust spread to occupied spaces.
Remove temporary barriers, edge protection, and exclusion signage methodically — store offsite or in designated non-occupant areas.
Brief all occupants in writing and verbally on cure times, maintenance requirements, and restricted-use periods before access reinstatement.
Conduct walkthrough with occupant representative or building manager to confirm safety and access readiness.
Wet-clean all contact surfaces (handrails, doors, balcony edges) disturbed during work before occupants return.
Isolate and label any areas still curing or under restriction — place prominent signage until cure time is complete.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reinstate occupant access until: site manager signs off that all debris is cleared, dust is controlled, all temporary protection is removed, and occupant brief is documented.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust or debris remains on balconies or common areas after final clean-up.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants cannot be safely briefed on cure times and restricted-use periods before access is restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: temporary barriers or protection systems cannot be safely removed without generating dust or creating trip hazards.

task_blocks_raw.task: Dismantle scaffold and demobilise from site
task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle scaffold under engineer supervision. Remove guardrails, edge protection, and temporary bracing. Clear all plant and materials from site. Leave site clean, safe, and locked.
hazards: Fall from scaffold platform during dismantling
Fall of scaffold components or materials from height onto workers or occupants below
Structural instability or collapse of partially dismantled scaffold
Crush or struck-by hazard during removal of guardrails and temporary bracing
Manual handling injury during removal and transport of heavy scaffold components
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from scaffold platform during dismantling
controls: Obtain engineer approval and written sequence for scaffold dismantling before starting — retain on site.
Verify scaffold is isolated from use — remove all access ladders and install 'Do Not Use' warning tags at all entry points.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 2 × scaffold height or 6 m radius around base — barricade with tape and position spotters at ground level during dismantling.
Dismantle scaffold from top downward following engineer sequence — remove guardrails and mid-rails before standards and ledgers.
Secure or remove all temporary bracing and ties — do not allow partial removal that destabilises remaining scaffold.
Use certified mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) or additional staged scaffold for dismantlers to work safely at height — harness and lanyard to certified anchor point above dismantler.
Collect all components at each level in designated drop zones — place in secured containers or on fall-arrest netting before lowering to ground.
Lower heavy components (standards, ledgers, frame bays) using gin wheel and rope or mobile crane with controlled descent — never throw or drop from height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start dismantling until: Licensed scaffolder or engineer has inspected scaffold condition and signed dismantling sequence.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lower or remove components to ground until: Exclusion zone is confirmed barricaded and spotters are positioned at base.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Scaffold shows signs of instability, cracking, or tilting during or after component removal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Wind speed exceeds 10 m/s or weather conditions (rain, low visibility) prevent safe work at height.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Exclusion zone is breached by occupants, vehicles, or unauthorised personnel.
admin: Confirm engineer approval and dismantling sequence document on site before work starts.
Brief all workers and spotters on exclusion zone, controlled descent method, and stop-work triggers.
Record dismantling start date, time, and licensed scaffolder name in site diary.
tell site manager and occupants 24 hours before demob commences — confirm occupants will remain excluded from demob area.
Obtain final walkover sign-off from site manager confirming site is clean, safe, and locked after demob complete.

steel-capped footwear, slip-resistant sole, AS/NZS 2210)
